title: Microsoft Intune: Windows quality update policies with per-type approval (Worldwide)
summary: The approval controls, Graph operations, licensing and policy defaults are supported by Microsoft documentation, and the dates match the roadmap record. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting LTSC guidance, complete the deferral path and cite the separate GCC roadmap item.

claims.claim: Approval methods and automatic deferral are configured at Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates > Create > Windows quality update policy > Basics > Settings in the Microsoft Intune admin center.
claims.quote: Under Settings, choose your approval method configuration for security updates, non-security updates, and out-of-band updates.
claims.fix: The route reaches the correct settings page but stops before the deferral control. Set the path to 'Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates > Create > Windows quality update policy > Basics > Settings > Make updates available after', retaining the note that this last setting is for automatic approval.

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies creates a policy with approvalSettings.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies

claims.claim: Manual approval uses Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates > Manage updates > release > Approved policies > policy > Approve.
claims.quote: Select the X of Y under Approved policies to see which policies are approved. Policies that aren't approved are marked as Needs review for that release.

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies/{windowsQualityUpdatePolicyId}/bulkAction supports the approval action.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies/{windowsQualityUpdatePolicyId}/bulkAction

claims.claim: Pause uses Devices > Manage updates > Windows updates > Quality updates > Manage updates > release > Approved policies > policy > Pause.
claims.quote:
Select the X of Y under Approved policies to see which policies are approved.
6. Select the desired policies and select Pause.

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies/{windowsQualityUpdatePolicyId}/bulkAction supports the pause action.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/windowsQualityUpdatePolicies/{windowsQualityUpdatePolicyId}/bulkAction

claims.claim: Role assignment follows Tenant administration > Roles > All roles > role > Assignments > + Assign > Basics > Admin Groups > Add groups > group > Scope (Groups).
claims.quote: Select the role you want to assign and then select Assignments > + Assign.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/deviceManagement/roleAssignments creates an Intune role assignment.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/roleAssignments

claims.claim: Intune audit logs are at Tenant administration > Audit logs.
claims.quote: Select Tenant administration > Audit logs.

claims.claim: GET /v1.0/deviceManagement/auditEvents reads Intune audit events.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/auditEvents

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The approval policy is admin-opt-in; devices without a policy continue standard Windows Update behaviour.
claims.quote: Devices without a quality update policy continue to receive quality updates through standard Windows Update behavior, using update rings and Windows Update client policies to control deferrals, deadlines, restarts, and notifications.

- Microsoft Intune Plan 1
- A Windows license that includes the Autopatch entitlement.

claims.claim: Quality update policies choose automatic or manual approval independently for each update type.
claims.quote: You can configure an approval method for Windows quality updates by individual update type.

claims.claim: Learn already documents the policies despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: Windows quality update policies allow you to manage Windows quality updates and supported .NET Framework updates for Windows devices.

claims.claim: Monthly security updates are an approval category.
claims.quote: Monthly security updates approval settings apply to both Windows OS cumulative quality updates and .NET Framework security updates.

claims.claim: Monthly non-security preview updates are an approval category.
claims.quote: Monthly non-security preview updates approval settings apply to both Windows OS preview updates and .NET Framework preview updates.

claims.claim: Out-of-band security updates are an approval category.
claims.quote: Out-of-band (OOB) security updates approval settings apply to both Windows OS security OOB releases and .NET Framework security OOB releases.

claims.claim: Out-of-band non-security updates are an approval category.
claims.quote: Out-of-band non-security updates approval settings apply to both Windows OS non-security OOB releases and .NET Framework non-security updates.

claims.claim: Approval settings cover OS updates and supported .NET Framework updates of the corresponding type.
claims.quote: Approval settings apply uniformly to both OS and .NET Framework update types under each release category.

claims.claim: The policy experience for .NET Framework updates applies only to Windows 11 devices.
claims.quote: For .NET Framework update management in Windows Autopatch, only Windows 11 devices added to the policy follow the quality update policy experiences.

claims.claim: .NET Framework 3.5 updates are outside these policies and use client-side settings.
claims.quote: You can't manage .NET Framework 3.5 updates through Windows Autopatch quality update policies. These updates don't appear in the quality updates workflow. Windows Update delivers these updates as standalone. Client-side settings govern these updates.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: New policies default monthly security updates to automatic approval.
claims.quote: When you create a quality update policy, the default approval configuration of monthly security updates is automatic.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Other update types, including out-of-band security, default to manual approval.
claims.quote: The default approval configuration of other updates is manual.

claims.claim: Automatic quality update deferral ranges from 0 to 30 days.
claims.quote: The allowed range is 0 to 30 days for quality updates.

claims.claim: The automatic deferral setting is called Make updates available after.
claims.quote: If you choose automatic approval, select Make updates available after. Specify the number of days to wait before updates are offered to devices.

claims.claim: Manage updates shows release details including severity and included KBs.
claims.quote: Select a Release name to see details, such as severity and included KBs. Use this information to review the payload before manual approval.

claims.claim: An administrator approves a release for selected policies.
claims.quote: Select the desired policies and select Approve.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An approved release can be paused.
claims.quote: You can pause an approved update at any time.

claims.claim: Pausing does not roll back devices that already installed the update.
claims.quote: Devices that already installed the update aren't rolled back.

claims.claim: A device assigned a policy receives only approved content for that content type.
claims.quote: When a device is assigned to a policy, it is enrolled in Autopatch for that content type, and only approved content is deployed to that device.

claims.claim: Manual approval deploys updates only after explicit approval.
claims.quote: This configuration provides full control, deploying updates only with explicit manual approval.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends automatic approval for security updates.
claims.quote: Windows Autopatch recommends automatic approvals for security updates and manual approvals for optional updates.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends manual approval for optional or non-security updates.
claims.quote: Manual approval: Recommended for optional or non-security updates in special cases.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that timely critical-update approval is essential to security compliance.
claims.quote: Use this setting with care, since timely approval of critical updates is essential to maintain security compliance.

claims.claim: Intune stores policy assignments rather than update packages.
claims.quote: Intune stores only the policy assignments, not the updates themselves.

claims.claim: Intune sends policy configuration to Windows Autopatch, which determines approved updates.
claims.quote: When you save a policy, Intune sends configuration details to Windows Autopatch, which determines which updates are approved for deployment.

claims.claim: Devices download approved updates from Windows Update.
claims.quote: Devices download approved updates directly from Windows Update, installing and applying those changes in accordance with Windows Update client policies.

claims.claim: Reporting requires allowing Intune access to enrolled devices' Windows diagnostic data.
claims.quote: To enable reporting for this feature, ensure your organization allows Intune to access Windows diagnostic data collected from enrolled devices.

claims.claim: Devices require telemetry at least at the Required level.
claims.quote: Telemetry must be turned on, with a minimum setting of Required.

claims.claim: Pausing revokes approval and prevents the release reaching new devices.
claims.quote: When paused, Windows Autopatch revokes the approval of the update, and no new devices receive it.

claims.claim: Devices can take up to eight hours to apply new pause settings.
claims.quote: Devices can take up to eight hours to apply new update pause settings.

claims.claim: Communication with Intune for new pause or resume instructions takes eight hours on average.
claims.quote: Windows devices take on average eight hours to communicate back to Microsoft Intune with new instructions to pause, resume, or roll back updates.

claims.claim: Policy and Profile Manager has read/write permissions on update policies.
claims.quote: | Policy & Profile Manager | Read/Write |

claims.claim: Autopatch Administrator and Autopatch Reader do not grant update-policy permissions.
claims.quote:
| Autopatch Administrator | No permission |
| Autopatch Reader | No permission |

claims.claim: Automatic approval offers updates after the configured release-relative deferral without individual manual approval.
claims.quote: Devices assigned to this policy receive an update after this many days since Microsoft releases the update.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cloud quality update deferrals override client-side update ring or CSP deferrals.
claims.quote: Deferral periods set in cloud-based quality update policies override any client-side deferral settings from legacy update ring policies or CSP configurations.

claims.claim: Assigning a device to a policy enrols it in Autopatch for that content type.
claims.quote: When a device is assigned to a policy, it is enrolled in Autopatch for that content type

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: After removal from every quality update policy, a device remains enrolled for 24 hours.
claims.quote: When a device is no longer assigned to any quality update policies, the device remains enrolled in Windows Autopatch for 24 hours.

claims.claim: After that 24-hour period, the device returns to Windows Update scans and client settings.
claims.quote: After 24 hours, the device is automatically unenrolled from Windows Autopatch for quality updates. From then on, the device receives updates based on Windows Update scans and client settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An existing policy's approval method cannot be edited; Microsoft instructs administrators to create another policy.
claims.quote: No, you can't change the approval method in an existing policy. If you need a different approval method, create a new policy.

claims.claim: Devices do not receive approved non-security updates when hotpatch is enabled in the policy.
claims.quote:
If a policy has hotpatch updates enabled and non-security updates are approved, will the device receive the non-security updates?

No, the devices won't receive non-security updates in this case.

claims.claim: Microsoft says to disable the policy's hotpatch setting to receive those non-security updates.
claims.quote: To receive non-security updates, disable the hotpatch update setting in the quality update policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Among several cloud-based quality update policies, the policy approving the latest release takes priority.
claims.quote: Device assigned to multiple cloud-based quality update policies. The policy approving the latest release takes priority.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A cloud quality update policy takes priority over a legacy hotpatch-only quality update policy.
claims.quote: Device assigned to cloud-based quality update policy and legacy quality update policy (with only the hotpatch update setting). The cloud-based quality update policy takes priority.

claims.claim: In that legacy-policy conflict, monthly security updates wait for automatic or manual approval.
claims.quote: That is, monthly security updates aren't offered to the device until you either manually or automatically approve them.

claims.claim: Devices must be Intune managed and Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid joined.

This policy type supports devices that are:

- Microsoft Entra joined
- Microsoft Entra hybrid joined

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra registered devices are unsupported for this policy type.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra registered devices aren't supported for any policy type that uses the same backend service as Windows Autopatch—including Feature updates, Quality updates, and Driver updates.

claims.claim: Supported Windows editions are Pro, Pro Education, Enterprise and Education.

This feature supports the following Windows editions:

- Pro Education
- Enterprise

claims.claim: Windows Enterprise LTSC is unsupported and Microsoft says to use update ring policies instead.
claims.quote: Windows Enterprise LTSC (Long Term Service Channel) isn't supported. Use update ring policies instead.
claims.fix: Replace the LTSC sentence with: 'The Intune Manage Windows quality updates page says Windows Enterprise LTSC is unsupported and to use update ring policies instead; the Windows Autopatch quality update overview and prerequisites pages instead say serviced Windows 10 and Windows 11 LTSC devices support the quality-update workload. Microsoft documentation therefore conflicts on LTSC support.' These three pages are already cited.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant service, wlidsvc, must be enabled and running.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant service (wlidsvc) must be enabled and running.

claims.claim: Devices require connectivity to Intune, Windows Update and Windows Autopatch endpoints.
claims.quote:
Devices must have internet access and be able to reach required Microsoft endpoints:
- Intune service endpoints
- Windows Update endpoints
- Windows Autopatch endpoints

claims.claim: Insider-build devices added to the policy are not enrolled for Autopatch quality updates and do not receive its approval settings.
claims.quote: If you add devices running Windows Insider builds to the approval policy, these devices won't be enrolled in Windows Autopatch for quality updates. Therefore, approval settings from the quality update policy don't apply.

claims.claim: Windows 10 ESU devices use policy approvals only for OS updates and client-side settings for .NET Framework updates.
claims.quote: Windows 10 devices enrolled in Extended Security Updates (ESU) continue to receive .NET Framework updates from Windows Update based on client-side settings. Therefore, quality update policy approval settings apply only to OS quality updates on those devices.

claims.claim: Policy management requires Policy and Profile Manager or a custom role with the listed Device configurations permissions and managed-device visibility.
claims.quote:
The Device configurations permissions Assign, Create, Delete, View Reports, Update, and Read
- Permissions that provide visibility into and access to managed devices in Intune (for example, Organization/Read, Managed devices/Read)
